why: The student says StdDraw.point(256, 256) lands in the middle because it uses pixels. That is the PixelCoordinates misconception: the default scale is the unit square, so (256, 256) is far outside the window and the point is not visible, and only the square appears in the middle.

concepts.quote: The square uses 0.5 as the centre
concepts.why: It correctly gives (0.5, 0.5) as the square's centre but never works out the square's size (side 2r = 0.5), so it covers only one aspect.
The answer makes no claim about double.

concepts.quote: the point uses pixels, so both are in the middle
concepts.why: It applies the wrong rule that point(256, 256) is the middle of the default window.
The default coordinates are the unit square, not pixels, so (256, 256) is outside the visible area.
The answer makes no claim about statements.
The answer makes no claim about empty statements.
The answer makes no claim about Math.round.
